params.fpl_basis: FLOOR(annual FPL / 12) before applying BBCE/130%/100% multipliers — the FNS/CalFresh published convention. Reconciled to CDSS ACIN I-46-25 (FFY2026) Attachment I; HALF_UP rounding here drifts +$1 at HH2/3/5/6/7/8 and breaks the published table (#606).

tolerances.note: $58 is SNAP QC program tolerance, not test slack.

meta.how_to_use: Facts are state-independent. Pick a state from expected_by_state to run; A/B rows: apply expected.variants[k].facts_patch then assert verdict. requires[] lists engine surfaces so a partial engine can skip unbuilt ones. integrity rows: feed agency_keyed, assert qc_should_flag.
caveats: Benefits computed by an INDEPENDENT oracle from facts (four-eyes), not citeable as PER; reconcile params.sd/allotment with production before trusting $.
SUA pinned to production for CA (663/170/20) and MA (914/556/64). TX/KS/AK SUA still illustrative — those states' expected_by_state benefits are null until production values land.
Generic dependent ages synthesized where unpinned; oracle/citation policy-sourced, never regenerate from the engine.
compute_benefit applies the homeless-deduction substitute ($198.99 FY26) per 7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(i) when shelter.homeless_deduction=true.

integrity.reason: Per 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1)(i), max-allotment / SD / FPL use ELIGIBLE-only HH size (size=2, kids only) for the undoc parent + 2 citizen kids case. Per 7 CFR 273.11(c)(3)(i)(A) count-all (CA election), the parent's $2000 wages count in full. Correct: $352. Prior expected $591 was authored against the pre-#434 engine that incorrectly used full HH size=3 for max allotment — the engine bug, not a policy choice. Both CA and MA pin to FY26 shelter cap $744 → both compute to $352.

averaged.note: $1,800 gross HH1: clears 200% ($2,610) and both TX's and IL's 165% ($2,153); denied under the federal 130% screen ($1,696-97) — KS/OH/GA (GA's regular-household screen stays federal 130% under TCOS categorical eligibility, same archetype as OH). AK cleared the federal-130 group before 7/1/2025 (#804); it is BBCE-200 (like CA/MA/TX/FL) effective 7/1/2025 and now clears here too.

recent_high_month.note: $2,200 gross HH1: clears only the 200% screen ($2,610). BBCE is not a boolean — TX and IL (both 165%, $2,153) deny; OH and GA (both federal 130%, $1,696-97) deny too (#609). AK is BBCE-200 effective 7/1/2025 (#804) and clears here too, same as CA/MA/TX/FL.

without.note: RE-AUTHOR: original 'DENY' expectation unreachable at gross income $0; max allotment forced per 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A). For a true child-support-deduction verdict-flip, base income must be set near the BBCE gross threshold and tested in a non-BBCE state. Tracking: #443

medical_30.note: under $35 floor per 7 CFR 273.9(d)(3) — engine zeros the deduction correctly; RE-AUTHOR: 'DENY' was unreachable because E/D household at $1250 RSDI lands net at $98 (CA) / $0 (MA), far under the $1305 net-test threshold even with no medical deduction. For a real medical-floor verdict-flip, RSDI must be tuned to ~$2070 so the household is marginally over 100% FPL net without the deduction. Tracking: #445

cash_to_household.note: countable unearned per 7 CFR 273.9(b)(2) — engine correctly counts the cash gift; RE-AUTHOR: 'DENY' was unreachable because $400 unearned for HH1 is far below CA BBCE gross threshold ($2610) and any net threshold. For a real countable-vs-excluded verdict-flip, gift amount must be ~$3000+ to cross the CA gross test. Tracking: #446
